article.title: Protect members’ retirement funds and invest in a clean and safe future for our children
article.author: California DSA
article.content: CalSTRS (California State Teachers’ Retirement System) is the world’s largest educator-only public pension fund, delivering reliable returns to investors while managing billions of dollars of assets. Teachers rely on their pensions to be invested responsibly: both with fiduciary responsibility and divesting from companies that contribute to genocide, apartheid, and environmental destruction. It is great that CalSTRS has formally acknowledged the need for a policy to mitigate environmental, social, and governance risks with investments. However, the current policy offers no enforcement mechanism to ensure teachers’ valued retirement funds are invested responsibly. CalSTRS must sell assets that contribute to war, genocide, apartheid, environmental destruction and adopt an ethical investment policy. Alameda County provides one example of an ethical investment policy to guide investments. The policy is comprehensive. It includes the language “Alameda County will not invest in companies that consistently, knowingly and directly facilitate and enable severe violations of human rights, as outlined in international law and the U.N. Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.” The CalSTRS board must adopt similar language to be a responsible steward of the billions of dollars of educators’ retirement funds. The following three educators are running to implement an ethical investment policy: Vinita Rajah —San Diego Educators Association Treasurer, CTA Retirement Committee Member, Vice-Chair of Asian Pacific Islander Caucus Mona Alsoraimi Espiritu —Tenured San Diego City College Faculty, served as Academic Senate President and Academic Senate Secretary previously, Student Engagement Climate Fellow Aidan Morris —Alameda Education Association Labor Council Delegate, Education in Managerial Economics DSA members can help promote an ethical investment policy and advance a new way of considering long-term responsible investing that protects communities and disallows funding apartheid and genocide. Help us gather hand-signed petition signatures from California teachers to get our candidates’ names on the ballot before December 18th. After the deadline, we will need to mobilize a mass education campaign to make California teachers at school sites across the state aware of the effort to implement an ethical investment policy and the importance in voting for a new vision for the CalSTRS board before the board election next November. To help with the campaign, download the petitions (see below), gather signatures from eligible CalSTRS members, scan and return to Aidan Morris via email ( aidanrmorris250@gmail.com ) by December 14th. Protect our Pensions. Invest in a future rooted in sustainability, racial equity, human rights, and peace. Petition for Vinita Rajah Petition for Mona Alsoraimi Espiritu Petition for Aidan Morris
